claim.why_it_matters: In the implicit description table the printed level-2 box encloses the three SUB-QUEUE comments. The markdown boxes SUB-QUEUE-1 correctly, puts stray box markers around the data-name-3 row and inside 'SUB-QUEUE-║2', and leaves SUB-QUEUE-3 unmarked, so the level-2 marking of the sub-queue items is garbled.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 665 (XIV-7) shows one rectangular level-2 box in the COMMENT column enclosing exactly the three lines SYMBOLIC SUB-QUEUE-1, SYMBOLIC SUB-QUEUE-2 and SYMBOLIC SUB-QUEUE-3; the data-name-2..4 PICTURE lines carry no box. The markdown (page-665.md lines 17-19) closes the box after SUB-QUEUE-1, opens a stray marker before the data-name-3 row, places another inside 'SUB-QUEUE-║2', and leaves SUB-QUEUE-3 outside any box. Both sources are quoted accurately by the claim. The text is all present, so the defect is the level-2 marking only: SUB-QUEUE-2 and SUB-QUEUE-3 lose their level-2 marking and the data-name-3 description gains a spurious one. The box sits in the COMMENT column, which the page's NOTE says is not part of the data description, and rule (4) carries the same level-2 marking for data-name-2..4 in prose, so the practical impact is limited; but the level marking is the standard's normative module-level designation, so the claim stands as described.
